name: New works since 2023: distractor discrimination, memory and refusal in single- and multi-object tracking

full_text_checked: Short screening. HTML full text read for the main tables/ablations of SAM2Long (Tables 6, 7, 10, main results), ODTrack (Tables 2, 4), MeMOTR (Tables 1-3, 6, 7), SambaMOTR (Tables 1-4, appendix Table F mentioned), SLAck (Table 1, Table 3 garbled), CAMELTrack (Tables 2-7, first 100k characters). Only abstracts for ADPTrack, arXiv:2311.02572 and arXiv:2508.14370. No code inspected; no supplementary material opened.
task_and_output: SAM2Long: semi-supervised video object segmentation (mask per frame from a first-frame mask). ODTrack: single-object tracking, box per frame. MeMOTR, SambaMOTR: end-to-end multi-object tracking by query propagation (boxes + IDs). SLAck: open-vocabulary MOT association. CAMELTrack: learned association module for tracking-by-detection (ID assignment). ADPTrack: look-ahead re-matching on top of a base tracker. 2311.02572: JDE tracker with occlusion-aware embeddings. FastTracker: vehicle-focused tracking-by-detection with occlusion-aware ReID.
data_and_independent_videos: SAM2Long: SA-V val/test, LVOS v1/v2, plus others (24 comparisons); training-free on top of SAM 2/2.1. ODTrack: trained on LaSOT, GOT-10k, TrackingNet, COCO; tested on LaSOT, LaSOText, TrackingNet, GOT-10k and others (seven benchmarks). MeMOTR: DanceTrack, MOT17, BDD100K (val). SambaMOTR: DanceTrack, BFT, SportsMOT. SLAck: TAO / open-vocabulary MOT (no BDD100K table in the text read). CAMELTrack: DanceTrack, SportsMOT, MOT17, PoseTrack21, BEE24. ADPTrack: MOT17. All test splits are unseen videos of the respective benchmarks.
target_size_and_input_resolution: SAM2Long: SAM 2 image encoder resolution (1024) [uncertain]. ODTrack: template 192x192, search 384x384, ViT-B (MAE init) / ViT-L. MeMOTR/SambaMOTR: Deformable-DETR full-frame inputs. CAMELTrack: YOLOX-x detections + BPBReID (Swin) crops + RTMPose/HRNet keypoints. Target sizes not reported per benchmark.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Native benchmark rates (DanceTrack/SportsMOT ~20-25 fps, MOT17 mixed static/moving cameras, BDD100K 5 fps labels in MeMOTR). ODTrack samples clips of 2-5 frames from ranges up to 1200 frames in training. ADPTrack reports largest gains for fixed cameras. No explicit camera-motion modelling in the read parts.
detector_and_exemplar: SAM2Long, ODTrack: no detector; first-frame mask/box. MeMOTR, SambaMOTR: built-in DETR detector. CAMELTrack: external YOLOX-x detector (ByteTrack recipe) + ReID + pose. SLAck: open-vocabulary detector. ADPTrack: base heuristic tracker's detections.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: SAM2Long: nothing trained (training-free tree over memory pathways). ODTrack: full ViT trained end-to-end with tracking losses on video clips; temporal token propagated between frames. MeMOTR: DETR + memory-attention layer, long-term memory as exponential moving average (lambda = 0.01), trained with MOTR-style set losses. SambaMOTR: Samba SSM per tracklet with cross-track synchronisation; MaskObs; 10-frame clips with gradients on the last 5. CAMELTrack: two transformer modules (temporal encoders per cue + GAFFE fusion) trained with association-centric training and data augmentation; detector/ReID frozen. ADPTrack, FastTracker: rule-based / dynamic programming; 2311.02572: trained occlusion prediction + dual embeddings.
controls_seeds_splits: Ablations on validation sets, single runs, no seeds or intervals in any of the read texts. SAM2Long: number of pathways P (Table 6), memory selection criteria (Table 7), uncertainty threshold (Table 10). ODTrack: token propagation, clip length, sampling range (Table 4). MeMOTR: long-term memory x memory attention (Table 6), lambda (Table 7). SambaMOTR: MaskObs, Sync, longer training (Table 4), MaskObs vs freezing (Table F). CAMELTrack: cue and fusion ablation with and without association-centric data augmentation, plus oracles (Table 5). SLAck: cue combinations (Table 1).

tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes for all (benchmark test/val splits). Target absence: SAM2Long yes implicitly (occlusion score > 0 required for memory write; LVOS/SA-V contain disappearance); ODTrack not reported; MOT works handle track death/birth but do not report a refusal metric. Similar distractors: DanceTrack/SportsMOT (MeMOTR, SambaMOTR, CAMELTrack) are similar-appearance datasets - yes indirectly; SAM2Long qualitative; ODTrack qualitative (Fig. 5). Occlusion: SambaMOTR MaskObs, SAM2Long, ADPTrack, 2311.02572 - yes; others not separately. Night/low light: not reported (BDD100K val in MeMOTR includes night but not split out). Sequential operation on own predictions: yes for all online methods; SAM2Long final pathway choice is retrospective.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanisms: (1) SAM2Long - keep P=3 alternative mask hypotheses with separate memory banks, score each by cumulative log predicted IoU, write a frame to memory only if IoU > 0.3 and occlusion score > 0, pick best pathway (final at last frame). (2) ODTrack - carry a compact learned target token from frame to frame as a prompt; gain +1.8 AUC LaSOT over no token. (3) MeMOTR - slow EMA long-term memory per track plus a memory-attention layer; gain comes from the combination (+2.8 HOTA on DanceTrack val). (4) SambaMOTR - per-track state-space memory synchronised across tracks; MaskObs skips low-confidence (<=0.5) observations in the state update instead of freezing (+1.3 HOTA). (5) CAMELTrack - learned association from multiple cues with temporal encoders; association-centric augmentation is worth +4.1 HOTA. (6) ADPTrack - look-ahead over future frames before committing a match. Proposed modification for us (not published): a FlyVis state update that is masked (not frozen) when observation confidence is low, and a slow EMA target memory in the readout, both evaluated on the applied matching decision.
transfer_limits: SAM2Long: requires SAM 2 masks, IoU and occlusion heads (RGB, ViT); the final choice uses the whole video, so the benefit is not available to an online tracker that must commit now; without masks, multi-hypothesis pathways on 721 grey hexals have no IoU-quality head to score them. ODTrack: large ViT on 384x384 RGB; the token learns appearance; an analogue on FlyVis is the recurrent neuron state itself, which already exists and was found not to beat its input. MeMOTR/SambaMOTR: end-to-end DETR trackers trained on full datasets; memory gains (+1.3 to +2.8 HOTA) are entangled with architecture and training length (SambaMOTR: longer training alone +1.3 HOTA); not transferable to a frozen YOLO26+ByteTrack environment without retraining the tracker, which is outside the FlyVis boundary. CAMELTrack: gains rely on ReID (Swin) and keypoints and on association training - a modernisation of the environment, not of FlyVis. ADPTrack: uses future frames (latency). 2311.02572/FastTracker: appearance ReID and road priors (FastTracker's lane/crosswalk priors conflict with the project's no-road-domain rule). Our setting: 30 Hz stream, 5 fps labels, moving rescaled crop, 34 motion types, targets ~9x12 lattice steps, find previous target among similar neighbours or refuse - none of these works tests a small motion-feature representation.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1: SAM2Long (presence via occlusion score separated from mask quality IoU - two heads; caution that the final choice is retrospective); SambaMOTR MaskObs (low-confidence observation not written into state). 5.2: direct evidence that memory write gating (SAM2Long Table 7, SambaMOTR Table F) and slow EMA memory (MeMOTR Table 7) help in RGB trackers; ODTrack shows a compact propagated token helps (+1.8 AUC). 5.3: CAMELTrack and SambaMOTR train on the association/ID objective - analogy for training on the applied decision; CAMELTrack shows training regime (augmentation) gives as much as cues. 5.4: CAMELTrack, SLAck, MeMOTR are direct association results; CAMELTrack Table 5 shows KF box alone 54.3 vs learned fusion 62.4 - a learned association can be a strong no-fly control.
candidate_node_change: Candidate (state node): masked state update of the FlyVis-derived target memory - during loss, frames whose observation confidence (presence) is below a pre-registered threshold do not update the target model/memory, while the FlyVis recurrent state keeps running (SambaMOTR MaskObs analogue, SAM2Long write rule analogue). Control without FlyVis: identical masked memory on eye-input (grey crop) features; control with stock FlyVis: same rule on stock ensemble outputs; also ByteTrack with no Z13 module. Minimal check: on train26 loss episodes, R1 rate of correct re-find and false re-find with and without masking; dev35 only once. Stop: if masking does not improve the correct-refind rate by a pre-registered margin with a paired bootstrap interval excluding zero, or if the eye-input control gains the same, stop before HOTA. Note: closely related to the already tried observation memory/query memory cards; the new element is only the write rule, so overlap with N16/N17 (DAM4SAM, SAMURAI write rules) is high - prefer to test it there.
strongest_objection: All gains are measured with large RGB backbones and trained trackers, without intervals, and mostly on datasets unlike ours; the memory gains in MOT are entangled with full end-to-end retraining. The parts that are causal and transferable (write gating, slow memory) were already the subject of N16/N17 and the project's memory cards, so this batch adds no new mechanism specific to small motion features.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed: SAM2Long (ICCV 2025), ODTrack (AAAI 2024), MeMOTR (ICCV 2023), SLAck (ECCV 2024); preprints: SambaMOTR (arXiv version read), CAMELTrack, ADPTrack, 2311.02572, FastTracker. Code repositories listed for SAM2Long project, ODTrack, MeMOTR, SLAck, CAMELTrack (not inspected). No independent replications checked. Overall: moderate for RGB trackers (consistent ablations), weak for transfer to FlyVis.
where_distinction_is_made: SAM2Long: separate decision heads - occlusion/presence score (object present) versus predicted IoU (mask quality); multiple pathways keep alternative hypotheses when uncertain (max |occlusion score| < 2 triggers diverse candidates), i.e. a map maximum is not trusted alone. ODTrack: only in the learned representation/token; no explicit absence. MeMOTR/SambaMOTR: in the learned query/state; detection confidence 0.5 gates state update (SambaMOTR); track death by score threshold. CAMELTrack: in the learned association module (cost over tracks x detections) - distinction between similar detections is learned from cue histories; refusal = no match above threshold. ADPTrack: by look-ahead over later frames.
feature_dependence: All depend on rich RGB features of large backbones (SAM 2 encoder, ViT-B/L, DETR, Swin ReID, pose estimators). The only cue close to ours is the box/motion cue in CAMELTrack (KF box 54.3 HOTA vs learned box temporal encoder 54.7 on DanceTrack val), which shows motion-only cues are much weaker than appearance+box fusion on similar-looking targets. No evidence for 34 motion cell types on 721 grey columns.
association_consequence: MOT works are the association itself: memory/state changes the track embedding used in matching (MeMOTR, SambaMOTR), or a learned cost replaces IoU/ReID heuristics (CAMELTrack, SLAck). SAM2Long and ODTrack are single-object and do not touch association. For us an external guard (Kalman gating, shift limit, confidence-gated update as in SambaMOTR MaskObs applied to the ByteTrack Kalman) could give the write-gating effect without FlyVis; CAMELTrack-style learned association is an even stronger no-fly alternative and would be an environment modernisation.
difference_from_tried: SAM2Long: differs from tried by keeping multiple hypotheses with separate memories over time (tried: ranking of 3 peaks per frame, framewise candidate identity) - but it needs future-frame selection for its final output. ODTrack: propagated compact token - not tried as such, but FlyVis recurrent state plus continued core training is the nearest tried analogue. MeMOTR: slow EMA memory - not tried as EMA (tried: memory of separate observations, query memory). SambaMOTR MaskObs: write gating by confidence - not tried explicitly (absolute confidence was tried as a decision, not as a memory write rule). CAMELTrack/SLAck: learned association over cues - outside the FlyVis boundary (environment). ADPTrack: look-ahead DP - not tried; uses future frames. 2311.02572/FastTracker: appearance ReID - no FlyVis analogue.
memory_write_policy: SAM2Long: write frame if predicted IoU > 0.3 and occlusion score > 0, searching back from t-1 until N frames; memory entries weighted 0.95-1.05 by occlusion-score rank. SambaMOTR: observation used in state update only if confidence > 0.5 (MaskObs). MeMOTR: EMA update with lambda 0.01 for tracked objects [uncertain - exact condition for update not read]. ODTrack: token overwritten every frame (no gating). CAMELTrack: feature bank of last 50 detections per tracklet. Others: not applicable / not read.
distractor_representation: Implicit in all read works (via learned representation or association loss); SAM2Long keeps alternative pathways which can include a distractor hypothesis but distractors are not labelled; MOT methods represent neighbours explicitly as other tracks.
refusal_evidence_horizon: SAM2Long: cumulative score over the pathway (accumulation, final choice at the end); SambaMOTR/MeMOTR: single-frame confidence threshold for track update and death; CAMELTrack: single-step association threshold with cue history; ADPTrack: look-ahead window over future frames.
loss_on_applied_decision: CAMELTrack and SLAck: yes (trained on association). MeMOTR/SambaMOTR: yes (set-based MOT loss on IDs/boxes). ODTrack: tracking loss on box/score map (intermediate for MOT). SAM2Long: no training.
association_entry_point: MeMOTR/SambaMOTR: track query/state update (state update). CAMELTrack/SLAck: matching cost. ADPTrack: matching decision after look-ahead. SAM2Long/ODTrack: not applicable (single object).
no_fly_control_equivalent: Confidence-gated Kalman update in ByteTrack (do not update on low-confidence or low-IoU matches); Hybrid-SORT weak cues (N18); a CAMELTrack-style learned association on box cues only; EMA ReID from MASA embeddings for the long-term memory analogue.
hard_subset_evaluation: No separate hard-distractor subset in the read works; DanceTrack and SportsMOT are themselves chosen as similar-appearance/complex-motion datasets; SAM2Long uses long-term benchmarks (LVOS, SA-V) as harder sets.
temporal_information_availability: Online, current and past frames only: ODTrack, MeMOTR, SambaMOTR, SLAck, CAMELTrack, 2311.02572, FastTracker. SAM2Long: per-pathway processing is causal but the reported output is the pathway with highest cumulative score at the last frame - retrospective selection over the whole video; an online variant (take the current best pathway) is not evaluated in the read text, so its reported gain is not the benefit of a correction our tracker must apply now. ADPTrack: requires several future frames before committing a match (latency of the look-ahead window).
depth_level: Short screening. None moves to full analysis: the transferable elements (memory write gating, slow memory, multi-hypothesis with presence head) are already covered by N16 DAM4SAM and N17 SAMURAI/UncTrack in full analysis; SAM2Long and ADPTrack depend on future frames; MOT memory gains are entangled with end-to-end retraining of the environment; CAMELTrack is an environment-level association and serves only as a caution/no-fly control.
